_provenance.kind: source-derived fixture — NOT a live capture
_provenance.why: search() returns 0 BOTH for a genuine zero-hit query AND for a rejected query; the two are told apart only by inspecting client.result afterwards. dedup/lpsn.py depends on that distinction, so both payloads are pinned here.

genuine_zero_results._note: client.py:190-192 — count present and 0 → 'Your search did not receive any results.'

query_rejected._note: client.py:185-188 — no 'count' key, error title/message instead → 'ERROR: <title> <message>' printed, search() returns 0
query_rejected.title: Bad Request

auth_expired_401._note: client.py:88-99 — a 401 whose message is 'Expired token' is refreshed and retried inside the client; any other 401 payload is returned as the result dict
